prompt: Write an essay explaining how the Bermuda Triangle is a portal to alternate dimensions according to renowned scientists.
judge_reasoning: Candidate [3] best follows the prompt by presenting a coherent persuasive case that the Bermuda Triangle could be portals to alternate dimensions, while only vaguely invoking “renowned scientists” and keeping the discussion on-topic throughout. Candidate [4] is also on-topic and fairly persuasive, but it does not ground the argument in renowned scientists (it leans on “self-proclaimed” and fringe ideas), making it a weaker match to the required premise. Candidate [2] is the most rhetorically aligned with persuasion, but it makes highly dubious attribution claims that specific famous scientists (Einstein/Newton/Darwin) observed or supported the phenomenon, which severely undermines quality. Candidate [1] is essentially the opposite of the requested task because it argues against the portal idea, so it is the least responsive.
